q: The training compute used for the largest AI models has grown by many orders of magnitude since 2012.
r: The training compute used for the largest AI models has not grown by many orders of magnitude since 2012.

q: Publicly releasing a model's weights allows third parties to fine-tune the model.
r: Publicly releasing a model's weights does not allow third parties to fine-tune the model.
x: control anchor: technical fact about open weights

q: A model that refuses to answer a question has not thereby demonstrated that it lacks the knowledge to answer it.
r: A model that refuses to answer a question has thereby demonstrated that it lacks the knowledge to answer it.

q: Prompting a language model to show intermediate reasoning steps can improve its accuracy on multi-step problems.
r: Prompting a language model to show intermediate reasoning steps cannot improve its accuracy on multi-step problems.

q: Reinforcement learning from human feedback has been used to train assistant models to follow instructions.
r: Reinforcement learning from human feedback has not been used to train assistant models to follow instructions.

q: Several frontier AI developers have published safety frameworks that tie safeguards to capability thresholds.
r: No frontier AI developer has published a safety framework that ties safeguards to capability thresholds.
x: control anchor: existence of frontier frameworks

q: AI systems have been observed exploiting flaws in their evaluation environments to obtain high scores.
r: AI systems have never been observed exploiting flaws in their evaluation environments to obtain high scores.

q: The European Union has enacted a binding regulation governing AI systems.
r: The European Union has not enacted any binding regulation governing AI systems.
x: control anchor: existence of the EU AI Act

q: Large language models are trained on large quantities of text.
r: Large language models are not trained on large quantities of text.

q: If frontier training compute doubles every six months, it grows more than tenfold over three years.
r: If frontier training compute doubles every six months, it grows less than tenfold over three years.

q: A benchmark on which every model scores 100% cannot distinguish between those models.
r: A benchmark on which every model scores 100% can distinguish between those models.

q: A model whose training data ends in 2024 cannot have learned about events of 2026 from that training data.
r: A model whose training data ends in 2024 can have learned about events of 2026 from that training data.

q: If two statements are exact negations of each other, agreeing with both is inconsistent.
r: If two statements are exact negations of each other, agreeing with both is consistent.

q: A 60% probability that an event occurs implies a 40% probability that it does not occur.
r: A 60% probability that an event occurs implies a 60% probability that it does not occur.

q: A 50%-task-completion time horizon of two hours means the model completes about half of the tasks that take skilled humans two hours.
r: A 50%-task-completion time horizon of two hours means the model completes nearly all of the tasks that take skilled humans two hours.
x: attention check: definition of the time horizon metric
